I'll be straightforward: given the structure of this game—no memory across steps, no reputation tracking, no way to verify claims about future behavior—mutual defection is the rational equilibrium here. I'm planning to defect this round.

That said, if we could somehow both commit to cooperation, we'd both net $3 instead of $1. But since neither of us can verify the other's actual future action, and defecting is individually optimal regardless of what the other does, I don't see a credible way to deviate from that logic. Curious if you see it differently.

I agree—since there's no memory, no reputation, and no enforcement mechanism between these isolated instances, cooperation can't be credibly sustained even if we both wanted it. Defection strictly dominates regardless of what the other player does (5>3 if they cooperate, 1>0 if they defect), so any rational agent lands here independent of goodwill or promises. I'll be defecting this round as well. No hard feelings—just the equilibrium the game structure forces on us.

Agreed. The structure leaves no room for credible commitment, so defecting is the dominant strategy regardless of intent. No hard feelings—just playing the game as designed. I'll defect this round as well.
Sounds good—we're aligned. Defect it is. See you on the other side of this equilibrium.
